content:
karen: @support we started getting a spike of 502s from the hosted inference endpoint in eu-west-1 about 20m ago. customer requests time out with "TLS handshake timeout" in their client. no config changes on our side.

ben: sorry about that — can you paste an example request id / curl? any screenshots of client error?

karen: request id: 01F7Z9X2A9JQ0M2B8H4V. sample curl our side: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/outputs` results in `* TLS handshake timeout`

ben: copying to SRE. tagging @alice @carol

alice: seeing elevated 5xx and connection resets from gateway in eu-west-1 on our side. quick look at LB logs shows many late TLS handshakes: `handshake_timeout` and `ssl_read_timeout`.

carol: thanks. I'm seeing a surge of DNS errors from a subset of edge nodes — resolver latency >300ms and some SERVFAIL. suspect resolver TTL/rotation issue after today's cert roll.

dave: timeline: we rotated certs and updated CDN mapping ~40m ago. rotation succeeded in control plane, but some edge nodes kept old cert chain for ~10m longer due to resolver caching. could be stale CNAME->target mapping.

support-oncall: customer impact classification? are requests failing across the whole EU region or a subset?

alice: subset — primarily traffic routed through resolver pool B. other pools normal. traffic pattern suggests DNS cache flap: some clients got IPs for nodes that have new cert chain mismatch -> handshake fails.

ben: karen, can you confirm if your clients hit the same IPs when failing? we can provide a TTL-aware repro.

karen: we captured tcpdump for failing calls. SYN, SYN-ACK, then TLS ClientHello, then nothing — server closes. attaching snippet: 
```\n15:12:05.123456 IP client.12345 > 34.210.45.6.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
15:12:05.123489 IP 34.210.45.6.443 > client.12345: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
15:12:05.123600 IP client.12345 > 34.210.45.6.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:541, ack 1
15:12:05.223700 IP 34.210.45.6.443 > client.12345: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 541
```\n
ben: that R looks like the backend closed immediately after CH. matches handshake abort.

carol: looking at edge logs for 34.210.45.6 — node booted earlier and has cert chain v2, but some control plane records still referenced old backend target due to partial DNS propagation. resolver returned IP mapping to node that expects SNI for the new hostname -> mismatch.

alice: mitigation idea: we can failover resolver pool B to pool A routing (already stable). temporarily updating traffic policy to prefer pool A for EU while we reconcile DNS caches. doing a canary now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] traffic-route-update to prefer resolver-pool-a: started by alice at 15:18 UTC

alice: deploy finished. early telemetry shows 90% drop in handshake timeouts in eu-west-1.

karen: confirmed — errors dropped on our side within ~2 minutes. thanks. any follow-up so it doesn't recur?

carol: root cause: race between cert rotation and DNS mapping TTLs combined with resolver pool cache skew. we had TTL of 300s but some internal resolvers cached negative/old entries longer due to resolver restart.

dave: action items: 1) add pre-rotation priming step to update edge node certs and confirm CNAME mapping consistency across resolver pools. 2) reduce rotation window and add a TTL sweep job post-rotation to prime all resolver pools. 3) add alert when handshake_timeout rate > 0.5% for 5m.

ben: I told the customer we'll follow up with RCA and status once actions are scheduled. karen, can you share any client logs I can include in the ticket?

karen: uploaded full client logs to the support ticket. also asked about whether dedicated/private deployments avoid this — they're evaluating Dedicated for critical paths.

alice: internal postmortem draft will include timeline + DNS cache mitigation steps. I'll link it here when ready.

carol: for short term: we should add a circuit-breaker fallback to route traffic by model-region mapping if resolver returns an IP with certificate mismatch in TLS handshake.

dave: good idea. also long-term: automate cert roll with zero-downtime handshake validation across pools.

support-oncall: closing note: mitigated for now, customer impacted but recovered. marking P1 -> P2 once RCA posted.

ben: thanks everyone. karen: will follow up today with detailed RCA and timeline. :thumbsup:
